results.name: first_example_side_extension
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples whose first example is the min or the max, yes rate for targets 1-20 beyond the span on the first example's side minus on the opposite side; observed > null means people anchor extrapolation on the first example more than the model's sticky first guess predicts, observed < null they favour the later examples' side.
results.code:
# name: first_example_side_extension
# description: For sets of >=2 examples whose first example is the min or the max, yes rate for targets 1-20 beyond the span on the first example's side minus on the opposite side; observed > null means people anchor extrapolation on the first example more than the model's sticky first guess predicts, observed < null they favour the later examples' side.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1); span = hi - lo
    dnear = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    is_ex = dnear == 0
    beyond = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi))
    interior = (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~is_ex
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    f = ex[:, 0]
    first_lo = (f == lo) & (k >= 2) & (span > 0); first_hi = (f == hi) & (k >= 2) & (span > 0)
    near = (beyond >= 1) & (beyond <= 20)
    below = t < lo; above = t > hi
    same = near & ((first_lo & below) | (first_hi & above))
    other = near & ((first_lo & above) | (first_hi & below))
    return rate(same) - rate(other)

results.name: near_total_rejection_set_fraction
results.description: Fraction of sets (with >=20 trials) whose overall yes rate is <=0.10; observed > null means people reject almost every target for some sets (all-or-none concept commitment) more often than the model's graded predictions produce, observed < null less.

results.name: ruleless_set_interior_yes
results.description: For sets of >=3 examples with no simple shared rule (mixed parity, no common last digit, no common multiple 3-12), yes rate on non-example targets inside the examples' span; observed < null means the model over-fills the interior of rule-less spread sets (people endorse an interval less fully than membership implies), observed > null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: ruleless_set_interior_yes
# description: For sets of >=3 examples with no simple shared rule (mixed parity, no common last digit, no common multiple 3-12), yes rate on non-example targets inside the examples' span; observed < null means the model over-fills the interior of rule-less spread sets (people endorse an interval less fully than membership implies), observed > null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1); span = hi - lo
    dnear = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    is_ex = dnear == 0
    beyond = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi))
    interior = (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~is_ex
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    e = np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=-1).astype(int); valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    par = np.where(valid, e % 2, -1)
    mixed = (np.nanmax(np.where(valid, par, np.nan), axis=1) != np.nanmin(np.where(valid, par, np.nan), axis=1))
    ld = np.where(valid, e % 10, np.nan)
    same_ld = np.nanmax(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ld, axis=1)
    common = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for mlt in range(3, 13):
        common |= np.all(np.where(valid, e % mlt == 0, True), axis=1)
    m = interior & (k >= 3) & mixed & ~same_ld & ~common
    return rate(m)

results.name: interior_yes_by_example_count
results.description: Yes rate on non-example targets strictly inside the span in 4-example sets minus in 2-example sets; observed > null means more examples make people fill the span more than the model predicts, observed < null means the model over-fills dense sets' interiors relative to sparse ones.

results.name: same_parity_interior_opposite_yes
results.description: For sets of >=3 examples all of one parity, yes rate on opposite-parity targets lying strictly inside the examples' span; observed > null means people include parity-violating numbers inside the range more than the model (which lets the parity rule dominate), observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: same_parity_interior_opposite_yes
# description: For sets of >=3 examples all of one parity, yes rate on opposite-parity targets lying strictly inside the examples' span; observed > null means people include parity-violating numbers inside the range more than the model (which lets the parity rule dominate), observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1); span = hi - lo
    dnear = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    is_ex = dnear == 0
    beyond = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi))
    interior = (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~is_ex
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    e = np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=0).astype(int); valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n_odd = np.sum(valid & (e % 2 == 1), axis=1)
    all_odd = n_odd == k; all_even = n_odd == 0
    tt = t.astype(int)
    opp = (all_odd & (tt % 2 == 0)) | (all_even & (tt % 2 == 1))
    return rate(interior & (k >= 3) & opp)

results.name: span_scaled_exterior_reach
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples, yes rate for targets 1-15 beyond the span in sets spanning >=40 minus in sets spanning <=15; observed > null means people scale extrapolation reach with how spread the examples are more than the model (fixed absolute reach), observed < null less.

# description: Among sets of >=2 examples, yes rate for targets 1-15 beyond the span in sets spanning >=40 minus in sets spanning <=15; observed > null means people scale extrapolation reach with how spread the examples are more than the model (fixed absolute reach), observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    k = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, axis=1); span = hi - lo
    dnear = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    is_ex = dnear == 0
    beyond = np.maximum(0, np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi))
    interior = (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~is_ex
    def rate(m):

results.name: interior_proximity_gradient
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples, for non-example targets strictly inside [min,max] example, yes rate when the nearest example is 1-3 away minus when it is >=12 away; observed > null means people still discount interior targets far from any example, which the model (no hesitancy inside the span) under-produces.
